title: ExtorQ - Linux Investigation
description: Linux hosts (asset_type linux_host): SSH authentication, sudo, accounts, systemd and cron persistence, HTTP probing and application logins. Sources: linux.journald, linux.auditd, linux.inventory, linux.nginx, linux.app (Linux SSH collector). host = the name inside the asset id. All text fields are attacker-controllable telemetry.

panels.title: SSH authentication failures by source IP
panels.description: Failed, invalid-user, pre-auth-closed and max-auth-exceeded sshd events per source address (VM-001 inputs). Source: linux.journald. Behind NAT every client shares one address.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time, ifNull(src_ip, 'unknown') AS source_ip,
       uniqExact(event_id) AS failures
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type IN ('auth.ssh.login_failed', 'auth.ssh.invalid_user', 'auth.ssh.preauth_closed', 'auth.ssh.max_auth_exceeded')
GROUP BY time, source_ip
ORDER BY time, source_ip

panels.title: Successful SSH logins
panels.description: Distinct successful sshd logins in the range on Linux hosts. Source: linux.journald. Compare with the failures: success after a failure burst matters.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT uniqExact(event_id) AS logins
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type = 'auth.ssh.login_succeeded'

panels.title: SSH failure sources
panels.description: Per host and source: distinct failure events, distinct (src_ip, src_port) connections (VM-001 counts connections, threshold 5 in 5 min) and attempted user names. Source: linux.journald.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, ifNull(src_ip, 'unknown') AS source_ip,
       uniqExact(event_id) AS failures, uniqExact(tuple(src_ip, src_port)) AS connections,
       uniqExact(actor_name) AS users, min(event_time) AS first_seen,
       max(event_time) AS last_seen
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type IN ('auth.ssh.login_failed', 'auth.ssh.invalid_user', 'auth.ssh.preauth_closed', 'auth.ssh.max_auth_exceeded')
GROUP BY host, source_ip
ORDER BY failures DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Recent SSH logins
panels.description: Successful sshd logins, newest first. Source: linux.journald. auth_method is empty when sshd did not report it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time, replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, actor_name AS user, src_ip,
       JSONExtractString(attributes, 'auth_method') AS auth_method
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type = 'auth.ssh.login_succeeded'
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 1 BY event_id
LIMIT 100

panels.title: sudo commands and failures
panels.description: sudo commands and denials, newest first. Source: linux.journald. Command lines are redacted at ingestion for known secret patterns; still treat them as sensitive.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time, replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, event_type, actor_name AS user,
       JSONExtractString(attributes, 'run_as') AS run_as, outcome,
       process_command_line AS command
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type IN ('auth.sudo.command', 'auth.sudo.failure')
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 1 BY event_id
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Local accounts and cron changes
panels.description: Local accounts that appeared or disappeared and cron configuration changes between inventory snapshots (VM-003 and VM-004 inputs). Source: linux.inventory. The change time is the snapshot that saw it, not the second it happened.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time, replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, event_type, actor_name AS account,
       JSONExtractString(attributes, 'uid') AS uid, JSONExtractString(attributes, 'shell') AS shell,
       resource_path AS path, JSONExtractString(attributes, 'sha256') AS sha256
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type IN ('account.user.created', 'account.user.deleted', 'persistence.cron.changed')
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 1 BY event_id
LIMIT 200

panels.title: systemd persistence changes
panels.description: systemd units created, modified, deleted or enabled and auditd watches on systemd paths: the VM-002 inputs. Sources: linux.inventory (snapshot diff), linux.auditd (watch key extorq_systemd). Both sources agreeing raises VM-002's confidence.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time, replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, event_type, resource_name AS unit, resource_path AS path,
       JSONExtractString(attributes, 'sha256') AS sha256,
       JSONExtractString(attributes, 'exec_start') AS exec_start, source_type
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND (event_type IN ('persistence.systemd.unit_created', 'persistence.systemd.unit_modified', 'persistence.systemd.unit_deleted', 'persistence.systemd.unit_enabled')
       OR (event_type = 'file.audit.watch'
           AND JSONExtractString(attributes, 'audit_key') = 'extorq_systemd'))
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 1 BY event_id
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Persistence events by type
panels.description: Distinct persistence-related events per interval (systemd units, daemon reloads, cron changes, auditd systemd watches). Sources: linux.inventory, linux.journald, linux.auditd.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time, event_type, uniqExact(event_id) AS events
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND (event_type IN ('persistence.systemd.unit_created', 'persistence.systemd.unit_modified', 'persistence.systemd.unit_deleted', 'persistence.systemd.unit_enabled', 'system.systemd.daemon_reload',
                      'persistence.cron.changed')
       OR (event_type = 'file.audit.watch'
           AND JSONExtractString(attributes, 'audit_key') = 'extorq_systemd'))
GROUP BY time, event_type
ORDER BY time, event_type

panels.title: HTTP responses by status class
panels.description: Requests seen by web servers and applications per HTTP status class. Sources: linux.nginx, linux.apache, linux.app. A rise in 4xx often means probing.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time,
       if(http_status IS NULL, 'unknown', concat(toString(intDiv(http_status, 100)), 'xx'))
           AS status_class,
       uniqExact(event_id) AS requests
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type = 'http.request'
GROUP BY time, status_class
ORDER BY time, status_class

panels.title: Route probing: routes with client errors
panels.description: Routes requested in the range, ranked by 4xx answers (HTTP-001 looks for many probe-like paths from one source). Sources: linux.nginx, linux.apache, linux.app. Route text is attacker-controlled; query strings are stripped at collection.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT http_route AS route, uniqExact(event_id) AS requests,
       uniqExactIf(event_id, http_status >= 400 AND http_status < 500) AS client_errors,
       uniqExact(src_ip) AS sources, max(event_time) AS last_seen
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type = 'http.request'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY client_errors DESC, requests DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Probing sources
panels.description: Client addresses ranked by client errors and distinct routes (probing indicators). Sources: linux.nginx, linux.apache, linux.app.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ifNull(src_ip, 'unknown') AS source_ip, uniqExact(event_id) AS requests,
       uniqExact(http_route) AS distinct_routes,
       uniqExactIf(event_id, http_status >= 400 AND http_status < 500) AS client_errors,
       min(event_time) AS first_seen, max(event_time) AS last_seen
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type = 'http.request'
GROUP BY source_ip
ORDER BY client_errors DESC, distinct_routes DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Application authentication failures
panels.description: Structured login failures and authorization denials written by web applications on Linux hosts (the lab-portal app's JSON log; APP-001 inputs). Source: linux.app.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time, event_type, uniqExact(event_id) AS events
FROM extorq.events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND asset_type = 'linux_host'
  AND event_type IN ('app.auth.login_failed', 'app.authz.denied')
GROUP BY time, event_type
ORDER BY time, event_type

panels.title: Services
panels.description: Current state: services discovered on Linux hosts (systemd units, processes, listening sockets) with their adapter and coverage. Source: v_services (Linux service discovery). Endpoint attribution: confirmed (socket owner observed), inferred (configuration or well-known port), unknown. Coverage: unsupported = no adapter; planned = extension point only, no telemetry; unmonitored = adapter not enabled; degraded = stale/failing (also when the discovery record is older than 1 h); monitored = enabled and fresh. The console/API also checks collector staleness per telemetry source.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT replaceRegexpOne(asset_id, '^[a-z0-9]+:', '') AS host, name AS service, service_kind AS kind, category, product,
       adapter_id AS adapter, adapter_support, monitoring_status,
       multiIf(adapter_support = 'none', 'unsupported', adapter_support = 'planned', 'planned', monitoring_status = 'unmonitored', 'unmonitored', monitoring_status = 'degraded', 'degraded', last_seen < now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR, 'degraded (stale record)', 'monitored') AS coverage, arrayStringConcat(arrayMap(e -> concat(JSONExtractString(e, 'protocol'), '/', toString(JSONExtractUInt(e, 'port')), ' ', JSONExtractString(e, 'exposure'), ' (', JSONExtractString(e, 'attribution'), ')'), JSONExtractArrayRaw(endpoints)), ', ') AS endpoints,
       arrayStringConcat(telemetry_sources, ', ') AS telemetry_sources,
       instance_count, last_seen AS discovery_refreshed, coverage_note
FROM extorq.v_services
WHERE present = 1
  AND asset_id IN (SELECT asset_id FROM extorq.v_assets WHERE asset_type = 'linux_host')
ORDER BY host, coverage, name
LIMIT 500
